approachQuestion.prompt:
Distance to a quote. A read-only nondecreasing array a contains n signed prices. For each of q integer quotes x return sum over all i of |a[i]-x|. Quotes need not be sorted.

Input: a=[-2,1,5], quotes [1,3]. Output: [7,9].

Constraints: 1 ≤ n,q ≤ 200000; -1000000 ≤ a[i],x ≤ 1000000. Duplicates are allowed. All products and totals fit signed 64 bits.

Which approach handles the complete task correctly and efficiently?

options.text: Build leading-zero cumulative sums P. For each x, binary search the first index k with a[k] ≥ x, or n if absent. Return x*k-P[k] + (P[n]-P[k])-x*(n-k).
options.feedback: Sorted order splits absolute differences into x-a[i] on the left and a[i]-x on the right. Boundary k also handles duplicates and quotes outside the array.

options.text: Return the absolute value of P[n]-n*x.
options.feedback: Opposite signed deviations cancel before absolute value: for [0,2] and x=1, it returns 0 instead of 2.

options.text: For each quote visit all prices and add their absolute differences.
options.feedback: This gives correct results, but repeatedly traverses overlapping candidates. The selected summary reuses their shared work.

details: Build leading-zero cumulative sums P. For each x, binary search the first index k with a[k] ≥ x, or n if absent. Return x*k-P[k] + (P[n]-P[k])-x*(n-k).

Sorted prices split at the first value at least x. Values before it contribute x-a[i]; later values contribute a[i]-x. Prefix sums combine those two linear expressions without scanning every price per quote.

“Build leading-zero cumulative sums P. For each x, binary search the first index k with a[k] ≥ x, or n if absent. Return x*k-P[k] + (P[n]-P[k])-x*(n-k).”: Sorted order splits absolute differences into x-a[i] on the left and a[i]-x on the right. Boundary k also handles duplicates and quotes outside the array.
“Return the absolute value of P[n]-n*x.”: Opposite signed deviations cancel before absolute value: for [0,2] and x=1, it returns 0 instead of 2.
“For each quote visit all prices and add their absolute differences.”: This gives correct results, but repeatedly traverses overlapping candidates. The selected summary reuses their shared work.

feedback.reason: Prepare sums once, then binary-search each quote's split point.
details: Building n+1 totals costs O(n) time and space. Each independent iterative binary search takes O(log(n+1)) worst-case time and constant extra state.
Use constant-time 64-bit arithmetic. Exclude read-only input and required output; include every described table. All loops are iterative, with no recursive stack or input copies.

Build n+1 cumulative totals in O(n). Each of q quotes performs a binary search over n values, costing O(log(n+1)), followed by fixed arithmetic on prefix totals. Total time is O(n+q log(n+1)). O(nq) rescans all prices per quote; O(n+q) omits the independent searches, while O(q log(n+1)) omits preparation.

The prefix table retains n+1 entries, giving O(n) auxiliary space; iterative search reuses a fixed set of bounds and totals. The constant-space alternatives omit the actual table. Supplied sorted prices/quotes and the q returned distances are excluded, but the newly built prefix table is included.
